title: Outdoor Movie Night Tech Essentials: Projector, Power, and Sound
summary: This This Old House segment inventories practical tech for outdoor movie nights, focusing on a projector-based setup, wireless connectivity, portable power, and weather-rated audio hardware. Viewers see how an outdoor-friendly projector can replace a wall-mounted TV, how Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi enable content and smart-home integration, and how a rollable solar-rechargeable battery bank powers the setup with real-world specs (about 1,000 Wh capacity and roughly 90 W load). The discussion covers solar charging options, USB/12V/120V outputs, and a portable speaker option versus permanent outdoor speakers, including IP ratings and UV protection as critical outdoor considerations. The segment also demonstrates smart outdoor plugs for scheduling and weatherproof outlets to manage the movie-night electronics. Collectively, it presents a practical blueprint for coordinating display, audio, power, and weather resistance in an outdoor entertainment environment.

sections.title: Outdoor projection options
sections.description: Ross and Kev introduce outdoor entertainment devices and note that projectors can be used outdoors with a screen or the side of a house to deliver high-resolution images, reflecting a shift away from wall-mounted TVs for exterior viewing.

sections.title: Connectivity and control
sections.description: The discussion covers how projectors connect via Bluetooth or Wi‑Fi, allowing data and control from phones and compatibility with smart-home platforms, enabling integrated outdoor viewing setups.

sections.title: Power and energy management
sections.description: Introduction to a lithium-ion portable power bank with about 1,000 Wh of capacity. The projector draws roughly 90 W, enabling over 10 hours of runtime on a full charge, with a solar-input option to recharge the bank for camping or RV use.

sections.title: Audio options and weather-rated hardware
sections.description: Comparison of built-in versus portable external speakers linked to the projector via Bluetooth or Wi‑Fi, plus the concept of docking a portable unit outside. It also discusses permanent outdoor speakers and the importance of IP ratings and UV resistance for outdoor gear.

sections.title: Wrap-up and practical tips
sections.description: Closing remarks with reminders to consider IP ratings, UV exposure, and scheduling; a light nod to planning outdoor viewing times (e.g., Sunday football) and subscribing for more content.
